Purpose: Read-only liveness probe (never touches Excel/COM).

name: workbook
description: Purpose: Open, close or save an open workbook through one lifecycle tool. Use when: you need to open an allowlisted workbook as a hidden working copy, close a workbook you are done with, or persist the working copy in place. Do not use when: you need Save As to a new path — use excel_save_as; the workbook is already open — reuse its workbook_id (workbook_read action='list'). Preconditions: an open workbook_id for close/save; path under an allowlisted root (EXCEL_VBA_MCP_ROOTS, default cwd + temp) for open; the original file is never modified. Parameters: action='open'|'close'|'save'; path (open); workbook_id (close/save); mode='execute' (default) or 'inspect'; read_only; save_changes; discard_changes; background. Behavior: open copies the file into work/ and opens it hidden; save writes the working copy in place (no path argument); close refuses by default when the workbook has unsaved changes: a clean workbook closes normally, while a dirty workbook is refused unless save_changes=true (save then close) or discard_changes=true (discard) is passed; save_changes and discard_changes together are rejected as contradictory. Result: WorkbookInfo (open/save), SessionStatus (close), or RunningJob when background=true. Next actions: workbook_read action='status' to confirm state; snapshot_create before further mutations. Example: {"action": "open", "path": "C:/data/report.xlsm"}

WorkbookInfo.description:
Workbook identity and top-level metadata (spec Appendix A, §7.1).

Two-path model (U6-E; plan_05 §5.4):

- ``path`` is the **working copy** actually opened by the server — the
  materialized file under the server ``work/`` directory (``wb.FullName``).
  All reads/writes and mutations target this copy; the original is never
  touched.
- ``source_path`` is the **original, allowlisted** path the working copy was
  materialized from. It is ``None`` when the workbook has no on-disk source
  (for example a snapshot restored from a baseline that itself had no
  source).

``original_name`` is intentionally **absent**: it would be redundant with
``name`` (the file name is identical for the working copy and its source),
so no separate field is exposed.

Examples:

- New open of ``C:/data/report.xlsm``: ``path`` =
  ``<temp>/excel_vba_mcp/work/<id>.xlsm``, ``source_path`` =
  ``C:/data/report.xlsm``, ``name`` = ``report.xlsm``.
- Writable working copy: identical to the open above; edits land in ``path``
  and ``source_path`` still points at the untouched original.
- Separate source/current: after ``excel_save`` the working copy at ``path``
  diverges from ``source_path`` (which remains the pristine original) until
  the change is deliberately persisted.

ControlEntry.description:
A Form Control or ActiveX control entry (spec §7.6 Controls inventory).

Form Controls and ActiveX controls live in different Excel collections and
expose different metadata, so this DTO carries both shapes of information:

* Form Controls (``ws.Shapes`` of type ``msoFormControl``) report
  ``control_type`` (button / checkbox / …), ``caption``, ``linked_cell`` and
  their ``on_action`` (the assigned macro, read verbatim, never executed).

  probable** event-procedure association. ``probable_procedure`` is a
  best-effort ``<sheet_code_name>_<control_name>_<event>`` guess (Excel's
  default document-module event handler naming); it is **not** a confirmed
  mapping and must never be reported as one. ``macro_mapping`` is
  ``PROBABLE`` for such an inferred association and ``UNKNOWN`` when no
  candidate can be formed.

name: excel_save_as
description: Purpose: Save an open workbook's working copy to a (possibly new) target path without rebinding the session. Use when: you need the working copy written to a different/new file (Save As), including overwriting the original source. Do not use when: you only need to persist the working copy in place — use workbook action='save'; the target is the open working copy (rejected); the source changed since open (STALE_TARGET). Preconditions: an open workbook_id; MUTATING approval on the target Approval gate (see xlvba://glossary). Parameters: workbook_id, path, overwrite_existing=false, overwrite_source=false. Behavior: flushes the working copy with wb.Save on the STA worker, then a pure-filesystem atomic temp->replace copy (never wb.SaveAs, so the session stays bound to its working copy and workbook_id/working copy/source are unchanged); a single <target>.bak preserves any previous target; an existing target needs overwrite_existing=true, the original source needs overwrite_source=true plus a matching source hash; skips the snapshot gate (Save As does not mutate the open working copy). Result: SaveAsResult (outcome 'ok' only after a final size+SHA-256 verify; 'unknown'/'error' fail-closed with backup_path). Next actions: workbook action='save' to persist the working copy; snapshot_create before further mutations.

Result of ``excel_save_as`` (U7; plan_05 §5.5, §9).

the target were verified. An interrupted or unprovable write reports
``"unknown"`` / ``"error"`` (never success) and, when a previous target was
preserved, carries its ``backup_path`` (a single ``<target>.bak``). The
session stays bound to its working copy (``wb.Save`` + a pure-filesystem
copy, never ``wb.SaveAs``): ``workbook_id`` / working copy / source are
unchanged by a Save As.

name: excel_recover
description: Purpose: Recover the owned Excel process (agent-directed). Use when: excel_health shows needs_recovery or a call is wedged. Do not use when: the server should not terminate a live pid on a deadline — it never auto-terminates; call this only when recovery is justified. Preconditions: a held, identity-verified owned process handle (RECOVERY class; see xlvba://glossary). Behavior: terminates the wedged owned EXCEL.EXE through the held handle (TerminateProcess + WaitForSingleObject), discards the working copies and rebuilds a fresh hidden instance; auto-allowed in full and restricted mode, audited, pid-scoped; fail-closed if no live handle is held. Discards the open working copies (originals are never modified) and does not roll back external side effects of any macro that already ran. Requires `confirm=true`; a missing/false confirm is rejected with CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED before any termination. Result: a recovery report; an interrupted operation is reported prior_job='unknown' and is never auto-retried. Next actions: re-open the workbook (the old workbook_id is invalid).

name: snapshot_restore
description: Purpose: Restore a working session from a snapshot. Use when: you want to roll the working copy back to a known baseline. Preconditions: an existing snapshot_id and the current workbook_id (required); the previous working copy is closed without saving once the restored copy is validated. Behavior: opens a fresh working copy from the snapshot baseline, validates it, then closes the previous working copy without saving — unsaved changes are discarded; does NOT undo external macro side effects (database writes, emails, network calls, files, printing). A missing/false confirm is rejected with CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED before the working copy is closed; a missing workbook_id is rejected with INVALID_RANGE (isRetryable=false). A failed previous-copy close does NOT fail the restore: the result reports previous_close='failed' with safe text and the previous copy stays open. Restoring the snapshot that is already the active restored baseline for the same original is rejected (reason 'same_snapshot'). Result: SnapshotRestoreResult — the restored WorkbookInfo (source_path rebound to the original) plus previous_close ('closed'|'failed'|'not_requested') and previous_close_error. Next actions: snapshot_create to re-baseline before further mutations.

outputSchema.description:
Result of ``snapshot_restore`` (plan_06 R1/R3; additive).

An additive wrapper over the freshly opened restored :class:`WorkbookInfo`
plus the disposition of the previous working copy's close (R1):

* ``previous_close`` is ``"closed"`` when the previous working copy was
  closed without saving, ``"failed"`` when the close raised (the restore
  **still succeeds** and the restored session stays valid — the previous
  copy remains open and the agent is told via ``previous_close_error``), or
  ``"not_requested"`` when no previous ``workbook_id`` was supplied.
* ``previous_close_error`` is safe, human-readable text (no secrets) when
  ``previous_close == "failed"``, else ``None``.

The restored ``workbook.source_path`` is rebound to the snapshot manifest's

(``workbook_sha256``) and the VBA ``project_source_hash`` the classification is

only holds while both are unchanged.

Use when: you need to resolve an address, read typed cell values/formulas, or inspect a Range's format/validation/conditional-format rules. Do not use when: you need to write values/formulas or change formatting — use range_write; you need to copy/insert/unmerge cells — use range_structural. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; sheet and address are required for every action. Parameters: action='get'|'read-values'|'read-formulas'|'get-format'|'get-validation'|'get-conditional-formatting'; workbook_id; sheet; address; offset + limit (read-values / read-formulas). Behavior: read-only; values are typed (empty/string/number/boolean/date/error) with no lossy string coercion; a mixed format/validation target is reported (never flattened) and unsupported conditional-format rule types are flagged rather than omitted. Result: RangeAddress (get), RangeValues (read-values), RangeFormulas (read-formulas), FormatInfo (get-format), ValidationRule (get-validation) or list[ConditionalFormatRule] (get-conditional-formatting). Next actions: range_write to change a value/format; range_structural to copy/insert/unmerge. Example: {"action": "read-values", "workbook_id": "<id>", "sheet": "Sheet1", "address": "A1:C10", "offset": 0, "limit": 50}

name: range_write
description: Purpose: Write values/formulas or set formatting/validation/conditional formatting through one mutation dispatch tool. Use when: you need to set cell values or formulas, apply a partial format update, or add/modify/delete a validation or conditional-format rule. Do not use when: you need to read a Range — use range_read; you need to copy/insert/unmerge cells — use range_structural; you need to delete cells — use range_delete. Preconditions: this tool does NOT snapshot — call snapshot_create first; then writable session + snapshot + approval Approval gate (see xlvba://glossary) + postcondition re-read. Parameters: action='write-values'|'write-formulas'|'set-format'|'set-validation'|'set-conditional-formatting'; workbook_id; sheet; address; payload (write-values / write-formulas); patch (set-format); spec (set-validation / set-conditional-formatting); mode (set-conditional-formatting: add/modify/delete). Behavior: write-values accepts a typed {kind, value} cell or a raw JSON scalar (string/number/boolean/null) stored as a literal by real JSON type only (no ambiguous coercion), and stores a leading '=' as text (use write-formulas for real formulas); the payload shape is validated against the target before any mutation (a valid range over 100000 cells is rejected as RANGE_TOO_LARGE); set-conditional-formatting mode='add' appends a rule and renumbers the sheet-wide priorities, so this tool is NOT idempotent. Guarded mutation (see xlvba://glossary). Result: RangeMutationResult (write-values / write-formulas), FormatMutationResult (set-format), ValidationRule (set-validation) or ConditionalFormatMutationResult (set-conditional-formatting). Next actions: range_read to verify. Example: {"action": "write-values", "workbook_id": "<id>", "sheet": "Sheet1", "address": "A1", "payload": {"rows": 1, "cols": 2, "values": [[1, 2]]}}

RangeWriteRequest.description:
Bounded 2-D bulk write payload for values/formulas (task_038 §3.3).

Rejected before any COM mutation when the grid exceeds the row/column/cell
ceilings or when ``values`` shape does not match ``rows`` × ``cols``. A
string beginning with ``=`` is **not** a formula: value writes store text;
formula writes use :class:`FormulaWriteRequest`.

Each cell accepts either a typed :class:`CellValue` or a raw JSON scalar
(WP-Range ergonomics): a string, number, boolean or ``null`` is coerced to a
literal :class:`CellValue` by real JSON type only (no ambiguous string
coercion — see :data:`ScalarValue` / :func:`coerce_cell_value`). The
normalization runs before field validation, so ``values`` always holds
:class:`CellValue` instances after construction while the input schema still
advertises the raw-scalar union.

Enforces the documented 255-character ``Formula1``/``Formula2`` limit before
any COM mutation. Formulas are opaque strings passed to Excel; never
evaluated in Python.

description: Purpose: Copy, insert or unmerge cells through one structural dispatch tool. Use when: you need to copy a Range to an explicit destination, insert cells with an explicit shift direction, or unmerge a merged area. Do not use when: you need to write values/formatting — use range_write; you need to delete cells — use range_delete; you need to merge cells — use range_merge. Behavior: copy requires a disjoint, shape-matched destination; insert rejects an omitted/disallowed shift and any ListObject intersection; unmerge discards merges. name: name
description: Purpose: Create or update a defined name (Named Range) in an explicit scope. Use when: you need a named range or constant in an open workbook, or you need to repoint an existing name's RefersTo. Do not use when: you need to delete a name — use name_delete; you need to read names — use name_read. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; writable session + snapshot + approval Approval gate (see xlvba://glossary) + postcondition re-read. Parameters: action='create'|'update'; workbook_id; name; refers_to (may be given with or without a leading '=', normalized); scope ('workbook' or 'worksheet' + owning sheet). Behavior: create rejects duplicate and cross-scope conflicts; update preserves scope and only rewrites RefersTo. Guarded mutation (see xlvba://glossary). Result: DefinedNameInfo. Next actions: name_read action='get' to confirm. Example: {"action": "create", "workbook_id": "<id>", "name": "Sales", "refers_to": "=Sheet1!$A$1", "scope": "workbook"}

NameTargetKind.description:
What a defined name refers to (spec §7.7: range vs non-range).

``RANGE`` names resolve through ``Name.RefersToRange``; every other kind is
classified heuristically from the ``RefersTo`` string without evaluating the
formula/expression (no ``Application.Evaluate``, no Python ``eval``).
NameTargetKind.title: NameTargetKind

outputSchema.title: DefinedNameInfo

name: name_read
description: Purpose: Read the defined names (Named Ranges) of an open workbook without mutating it. Use when: you need every defined name or one name's metadata by name + scope. Do not use when: you need to create/update a name — use name; you need to delete a name — use name_delete. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; name + scope are required for get (sheet also required for a worksheet scope). Parameters: action='list'|'get'; workbook_id; name (get); scope (get); sheet (get, worksheet scope). Behavior: read-only; list returns one entry per defined name across workbook and worksheet scopes with scope, NameLocal, Visible, RefersTo/RefersToLocal and target_kind (range with sheet+address, constant, formula, external, error or unknown); get returns one DefinedNameInfo. Result: list[DefinedNameInfo] (list) or DefinedNameInfo (get). Next actions: name action='create' to add a name; name_delete to remove one. Example: {"action": "get", "workbook_id": "<id>", "name": "Sales", "scope": "workbook"}

name: shape
description: Purpose: List, read or assign the OnAction of drawing shapes of an open workbook. Use when: you need the shape inventory, one shape's metadata, or you need to set/clear a shape's OnAction macro (the macro is NOT executed). Do not use when: you need Form/ActiveX controls — use control. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; name is required for get and set-on-action; macro_name is required for set-on-action; set-on-action is a Guarded mutation (see xlvba://glossary). Parameters: action='list'|'get'|'set-on-action'; workbook_id; name (get, set-on-action); macro_name (set-on-action; "" clears it). Behavior: list returns one entry per Worksheet.Shapes item (name, kind, on_action read verbatim, visibility, position/size, best-effort text); get returns one ShapeInfo; set-on-action writes Shape.OnAction only. Result: list[ShapeInfo] (list) or ShapeInfo (get / set-on-action). Next actions: shape action='get' to confirm; control for Form/ActiveX controls. Example: {"action": "set-on-action", "workbook_id": "<id>", "name": "btnSave", "macro_name": "SaveData"}

ShapeInfo.description:
A drawing-layer shape entry (spec §7.6 Shapes inventory).

One entry per ``Worksheet.Shapes`` item. ``kind`` is derived from
``Shape.Type`` (``msoShapeType``); ``on_action`` is the shape's ``OnAction``
text read verbatim — **the assigned macro is never executed**. Coordinates
and size are Excel points; ``top``/``left``/``width``/``height`` are ``None``
when the property is unavailable. ``text`` is a best-effort rendering of the
shape's text frame (never ``None`` when a text frame exists but is empty:
an empty string is meaningful). ``control_format`` is ``True`` only when the
shape exposes an Excel ``ControlFormat`` object (Form Controls); ActiveX /
plain shapes report ``None``.

control_format.description: True when the shape exposes an Excel ControlFormat (Form Control).
control_format.title: Control Format

notes.description: Diagnostics for properties that could not be read.

The Excel ``MsoShapeType`` enumeration is mapped to this closed vocabulary.
``FormControl`` and ``OLEControlObject`` classify as their dedicated kinds so
callers can tell a Form Control / ActiveX object from a plain drawing shape;
every other drawing type (AutoShape, TextBox, Group, Picture, …) is ``SHAPE``.

name: control
description: Purpose: List, read or assign the OnAction of Form Controls / ActiveX controls of an open workbook. Use when: you need the control inventory, one control's metadata, or you need to set/clear a Form Control's OnAction macro (the macro is NOT executed). Do not use when: you need drawing shapes — use shape. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; name is required for get and set-on-action; macro_name is required for set-on-action; set-on-action is a Guarded mutation (see xlvba://glossary). Parameters: action='list'|'get'|'set-on-action'; workbook_id; name (get, set-on-action); macro_name (set-on-action; "" clears it). Behavior: list reports Form Controls (control_type, caption, linked_cell, on_action) and ActiveX controls (prog_id, inferred/probable event procedure); get returns one ControlEntry; set-on-action writes OnAction on a Form Control only (ActiveX controls are rejected — no OnAction). Result: list[ControlEntry] (list) or ControlEntry (get / set-on-action). Next actions: control action='get' to confirm; shape for drawing shapes. Example: {"action": "set-on-action", "workbook_id": "<id>", "name": "cmdRun", "macro_name": "RunReport"}

ControlEntry.description:
A Form Control or ActiveX control entry (spec §7.6 Controls inventory).

Form Controls and ActiveX controls live in different Excel collections and
expose different metadata, so this DTO carries both shapes of information:

* Form Controls (``ws.Shapes`` of type ``msoFormControl``) report
  ``control_type`` (button / checkbox / …), ``caption``, ``linked_cell`` and
  their ``on_action`` (the assigned macro, read verbatim, never executed).
* ActiveX controls (``ws.OLEObjects``) report ``prog_id`` plus an **inferred,
  probable** event-procedure association. ``probable_procedure`` is a
  best-effort ``<sheet_code_name>_<control_name>_<event>`` guess (Excel's
  default document-module event handler naming); it is **not** a confirmed
  mapping and must never be reported as one. ``macro_mapping`` is
  ``PROBABLE`` for such an inferred association and ``UNKNOWN`` when no
  candidate can be formed.

probable_procedure.description: Inferred ActiveX event procedure (probable, not confirmed).
probable_procedure.title: Probable Procedure

notes.description: Diagnostics for properties that could not be read.
notes.title: Notes

ControlEntry.title: ControlEntry

MacroMappingStatus.description: Whether a control OnAction maps to a resolved VBA procedure (spec §7.4).

name: xlvba_environment
description: Purpose: Report the server's access mode, policy, build and capabilities without touching COM. Use when: you need to know the access mode, whether mutations need a grant, the snapshot gate, path roots, macro gates or the honest build (always null). Do not use when: you need worker/session liveness — use excel_health; for a pure liveness probe use server_health. Preconditions: none (non-COM, side-effect-free, read-only). Behavior: never creates snapshots, grants or classifications; policy.classification_is_authorization=false is stated explicitly; build is null (no 4-part source); excel.available=false when the worker is down. Result: EnvironmentReport (server, excel, capabilities, policy, glossary_uri, workbooks). Next actions: workbook action='open' / snapshot_create as the policy requires. Capabilities (this server provides): VBA project access, macros, pivot tables (database-source; manual filters), background jobs, recovery, and non-activating compile diagnostics — NOT compilation (sourced from EnvironmentCapabilities). Routing is capability-based advice only: this server does NOT detect whether any other MCP server is installed or connected. Prefer xlvba when the task needs the working-copy lifecycle, session-aware operations, snapshot/guarded mutation, VBA/macro management, pivot/cache diagnostics, background jobs, Excel health/recovery, or policy-aware execution. Use excel-mcp when it exposes an equivalent supported operation that does NOT need xlvba's session/snapshot/working-copy/recovery guarantees. Matrix: working copy or session binding -> xlvba; snapshot + guarded mutation -> xlvba; VBA/macro/pivot-cache/background/recovery -> xlvba; plain cell/range/sheet op with no session guarantee needed -> excel-mcp. Examples: 'read one cell from a disposable file' -> excel-mcp; 'edit a cell, snapshot, then recover the owned Excel process' -> xlvba.

AccessMode.description:
Server access policy controlling approval behavior (task_b2, fix_002).

Shared, zero-dependency vocabulary consumed by the approval policy and the
server configuration. ``FULL`` authorizes mutating/executing operations by
default (no per-action grant); ``RESTRICTED`` keeps the deny-by-default gate
and is an explicit opt-in. Neither mode bypasses PathPolicy / Office-trust /
snapshot / audit.
AccessMode.title: AccessMode

EnvironmentCapabilities.description: Capability flags derived from registration + status enums (plan_03 §6.1).

non_activating_compile.description: Always false on the validated build (compile never returns compiled/error).
non_activating_compile.title: Non Activating Compile

EnvironmentCapabilities.title: EnvironmentCapabilities

EnvironmentExcelInfo.description:
Owned Excel instance summary (``xlvba_environment.excel``).

``build`` is **always** ``None`` — there is no 4-part build source, so the
field is honest ``null`` and can never be fabricated. ``target_build`` is a
labelled design-time constant only (not a detected build).
``application_version`` is a non-COM best-effort value taken from an open
workbook's cached ``Application.Version`` (or ``None`` when none is open).
``vbom_available`` is ``None`` at server level (no workbook model is built).

build.title: Build

target_build.title: Target Build

name: workbook_file_read
description: Purpose: Read workbook metadata, a page of worksheet rows, or saved PivotCache records from an immutable snapshot file via non-COM streaming OOXML parsing. Use when: you need large-sheet rows, workbook structure, or saved pivot-cache records without materializing the sheet or occupying the single-STA COM worker. Do not use when: you need the live working copy or the displayed pivot result — use range_read / pivot_read; you need VBA source — use vba_read. Preconditions: an open workbook_id (or an explicit snapshot_id); when snapshot_id is omitted a fresh snapshot is created as the immutable input. Parameters: action='metadata'|'sheet-rows'|'pivot-cache-records'; workbook_id; sheet (sheet-rows); offset (0-based); limit; snapshot_id; cache_index (pivot-cache-records, 1-based). Behavior: read-only, bounded and streamed in a worker thread; the single-STA COM worker is never occupied; a cache with no saved local records yields an empty page with page.reason='unsupported_source'. Result: OoxmlMetadata (metadata), OoxmlSheetPage (sheet-rows) or OoxmlPivotCachePage (pivot-cache-records). Next actions: range_read / pivot_read for the live view; data_export to stream a result to a file. Example: {"action": "sheet-rows", "workbook_id": "<id>", "sheet": "Sheet1", "offset": 0, "limit": 1000}

CellValue.description: A typed cell value for read-only output assertions (spec §7.6, §9.3).
CellValue.title: CellValue

CellValueKind.description: Cell value type for read-only output assertions (spec §7.6, §9.3).
CellValueKind.title: CellValueKind

OoxmlInputInfo.description:
Provenance of a non-COM OOXML read (WP-E1).

``input_sha256`` is the SHA-256 of the immutable snapshot file the data was
parsed from; ``snapshot_id`` is the snapshot used (the freshly created one,
or the caller-supplied one). ``source`` is always ``"snapshot"`` — the live
working copy and the original are never read.
OoxmlInputInfo.title: OoxmlInputInfo

OoxmlMetadata.description:
Workbook metadata read non-COM from an immutable snapshot (WP-E1).

Lists the sheets (name/part/hidden/order via :class:`OxmlSheetMeta`), the
workbook defined names and the table-part count. Never carries cell data.
OoxmlMetadata.title: OoxmlMetadata

OoxmlPivotCacheMeta.description:
Freshness / completeness metadata of a saved PivotCache (WP-E2).

Describes the **saved** cache (not the PivotTable's displayed result and not
the live source): ``record_count`` is the definition's ``recordCount`` (when
present), ``save_data`` is the ``saveData`` flag (``False`` means the cache
stored no local records), ``refresh_on_load`` / ``refresh_date`` report the
cache's refresh freshness, and ``has_records_part`` is ``True`` only when a
``pivotCacheRecords`` part is actually present in the snapshot.
OoxmlPivotCacheMeta.title: OoxmlPivotCacheMeta

OoxmlPivotCachePage.description:
A bounded page of typed **saved** PivotCache records (WP-E2).

``values`` holds one inner list per record, field-aligned; every cell is a
typed :class:`CellValue` (shared-item indices resolved against the cache's
shared-items table). The grid is bounded by :data:`MAX_RESPONSE_CELLS` and
``len(values) == rows``. ``page.source`` is ``"cache"`` and ``page.version`` is
``0`` (a snapshot is immutable). When the cache has no local records
(``saveData="0"`` / OLAP / Data Model) the page is empty with
``page.reason == "unsupported_source"`` and ``meta.has_records_part`` is
``False`` — the records are never fabricated.
OoxmlPivotCachePage.title: OoxmlPivotCachePage

OoxmlSheetPage.description:
A bounded page of typed worksheet rows read from a snapshot (WP-E1).

``values`` holds one inner list per row, each aligned by column index; every
cell is a typed :class:`CellValue`. The grid is bounded by
:data:`MAX_RESPONSE_CELLS` and ``len(values) == rows``. ``page.source`` is
``"snapshot"`` and ``page.version`` is ``0`` (a snapshot is immutable).
OoxmlSheetPage.title: OoxmlSheetPage

OxmlSheetMeta.description:
One worksheet's structural metadata from the snapshot (WP-E1).

``part`` is the package part path (e.g. ``xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml``);
``hidden`` is ``True`` for hidden / very-hidden sheets; ``rows_hint`` is an
optional best-effort row count (``None`` when not cheaply known).
OxmlSheetMeta.title: OxmlSheetMeta

PageInfo.description:
Large-data completeness + version block (additive; large-data contract §2).

Attached to paged reads so an agent never mistakes partial data for complete
data. ``version`` is the workbook content version the page belongs to;
``source`` is ``"live"`` (open workbook), ``"snapshot"`` (immutable SaveCopyAs
file) or ``"cache"`` (saved PivotCache records). ``reason`` is set only when
the page is empty for a reason other than ``no_data``.

offset.description: 0-based row/item offset of the first returned item.
offset.title: Offset

total.description: Total available when safely known, else None.
total.title: Total

has_more.description: More items exist beyond this page.
has_more.title: Has More

complete.description: True iff every item has been delivered (returned == total).
complete.title: Complete

truncated.description: True iff a single response was cut by a limit.
truncated.title: Truncated

version.description: Workbook content version of this page.
version.title: Version

source.description: Data origin: live workbook, immutable snapshot, or saved PivotCache.
source.title: Source

reason.description: Set only when the page is empty for a reason other than 'no data'.
reason.title: Reason

PageInfo.title: PageInfo

name: data_export
description: Purpose: Stream a large dataset — a worksheet Range, an Excel Table (ListObject) data body or a PivotTable's rendered result — to a CSV / JSONL file artifact with bounded memory, returning only compact metadata. Use when: the data is too large to return inline and you need it written to a file artifact. Do not use when: you need the data inline (use range_read / table_read / pivot_read) or a non-file artifact — no existing tool streams to a file. Preconditions: an open workbook_id; the source selector for source_kind. Parameters: workbook_id; source_kind='range'|'table'|'pivot-result'; sheet + address (range); table (table); pivot_table (pivot-result); fmt='csv'|'jsonl'; limit_rows. Behavior: each page is read and written straight to the artifact stream so only one page is held in memory; the data is never returned inline; non-destructive and idempotent (each call writes a new artifact). Result: DataExportResult (artifact path, rows, bytes, sha256, truncated/complete). Next actions: workbook_file_read to page the source; range_read for a bounded inline view. Example: {"workbook_id": "<id>", "source_kind": "range", "sheet": "Sheet1", "address": "A1:C100000", "fmt": "csv"}

outputSchema.description:
Compact result of a large-data file export (WP-F).

``path`` is the stored artifact file (CSV / JSONL); the data is never returned
inline. ``rows`` is the number of data rows written (excluding a CSV header),
``bytes`` / ``sha256`` describe the written file, ``complete`` is ``True`` iff
every source row was delivered, ``truncated`` is ``True`` iff the export was cut
by ``limit_rows`` or the ``max_export_rows`` ceiling, ``source`` is the source
kind (``"range"`` / ``"table"`` / ``"pivot-result"``) and ``source_version`` is
the workbook content version the export was bound to (captured at start).
``input_sha256`` is the SHA-256 of the immutable snapshot file the export read
from (``None`` only on a legacy path that did not bind a snapshot).
outputSchema.title: DataExportResult
